questions.q: What does the `pool` key in azure-pipelines.yml control?
options: Which branch triggers the pipeline
The agent (hosted or self-hosted) the job runs on
The list of environment variables available to the job
Which service connection the pipeline uses
questions.explain: pool selects the agent a job runs on, such as the Microsoft-hosted ubuntu-latest image.

questions.q: What's the difference between a `task` step and a `script` step?
options: There is no functional difference, only naming
A task is a pre-built, versioned catalog building block; a script runs a raw shell command directly
A script step can only run on Windows agents
A task step cannot access pipeline variables
questions.explain: Tasks like UseNode@3 or Docker@2 are maintained, versioned building blocks; script steps run arbitrary shell commands for anything a task doesn't cover.

questions.q: In the Docker@2 task, what does `containerRegistry` reference?
options: A literal username and password typed directly into the YAML file
A service connection — a stored, authenticated link to the registry
The name of the Kubernetes cluster
A variable group in the Library
questions.explain: containerRegistry points at a service connection, the authenticated link to the registry covered in full in Lesson 14 — not a credential pasted into the YAML.

questions.q: Why tag the built container image with $(Build.BuildId) instead of just `latest`?
options: Build.BuildId makes the image smaller
latest tags are not supported by Azure Container Registry
A unique build ID tag keeps every build traceable instead of silently overwriting the previous image
It is required syntax and has no practical purpose
questions.explain: Tagging with the built-in Build.BuildId variable gives every build a unique, traceable tag rather than overwriting a shared latest tag each run.

questions.q: What do the `trigger` and `pr` blocks each control?
options: trigger controls CI runs on push; pr controls validation builds on pull requests
They are interchangeable and do the same thing
trigger controls pull requests; pr controls scheduled runs
Both only apply to Classic pipelines, not YAML
questions.explain: trigger defines what starts a run automatically on a push to the listed branches, while pr defines validation builds that run against pull requests targeting those branches.
